title: WebMCP vs MCP: Which Do You Need for Agents?
excerpt: WebMCP is for websites that expose in-page tools. MCP is for servers your agent connects to across apps. Here is how to choose — and where to browse each on Influzer.
coverImageAlt: Diagram contrasting in-page WebMCP tools with external MCP servers
contentHtml:
Short answer: use WebMCP when the agent is already on a website and should call that site’s declared tools. Use MCP when the agent needs durable integrations — GitHub, Postgres, Slack, scrapers — that travel with the client.

The names collide. The layers do not. Mixing them up wastes a week of “why won’t my site show up as an MCP server?” or “why can’t my agent book on this page?”

Side-by-side

WebMCPMCP (servers)
What it isWebsite exposes in-page tools (schemas + intents)External tool server over stdio/HTTP
Where it runsIn the browser, on the originLocal process or remote host
DiscoveryUsually after visiting the pageConfig / directory / install URL
Best forSearch, forms, booking, checkout on your siteRepos, APIs, SaaS, automation across apps
Browse on Influzer/webmcp/mcp

When you need WebMCP

Choose WebMCP if:

  • You own a product website and agents already land there
  • DOM guessing fails on multi-step flows (booking, support forms, filters)
  • You want actions to stay visible on your UI with your brand and confirmations

Start by browsing live examples in the WebMCP directory, try Influzer’s own WebMCP, then scan and list your site.

When you need MCP servers

Choose MCP if:

  • The agent must reach systems that are not “this webpage”
  • You need the same tools in Cursor, Claude, or ChatGPT across sessions
  • You care about handshake checks, install snippets, and allowlists

Search the MCP server directory, prefer handshake-checked remotes, and submit your server when you ship one. For setup from inside the agent, use Discovery.

You will often need both

A realistic stack:

  1. MCP for GitHub + docs + CRM
  2. WebMCP on your marketing and app origins so browser agents stop thrashing the DOM

They are complementary. WebMCP does not replace Postgres MCP. MCP does not magically teach agents your checkout page.

Common mistakes

  • “Our site is an MCP server.” Usually false — unless you host a separate MCP endpoint. Publish WebMCP tools on the page, or stand up a real MCP server. See also your website is not an MCP server.
  • “MCP Apps = WebMCP.” No — different surfaces. Read MCP Apps are not WebMCP.
  • Skipping verification. For MCP remotes, run a handshake before you allowlist. For WebMCP, inspect the tool list on the live page.

Decision checklist

  1. Is the work on a specific website UI? → WebMCP first
  2. Is the work across systems / lasting tools? → MCP servers
  3. Shipping either? → List it: WebMCP submit or MCP submit

Quick answers

Is WebMCP an official W3C standard yet?

It is an active web-platform / Chrome early path — treat docs as evolving. Product value still holds: declared tools beat DOM guessing.

Can one product offer both?

Yes. Many will: WebMCP on the site, MCP for partner/agent integrations.

Where should I start as a buyer?

Browse WebMCP sites for agent-ready web UX. Browse MCP servers for stack connectors. Then connect Discovery so search stays inside the agent.

Bottom line: WebMCP = site tools. MCP = stack tools. Pick the layer that matches the job — then use Influzer to find or publish it.
